steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Boolean algebra uses variables with values 0 or 1; operations are AND (·), OR (+) and NOT (overbar).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Identity laws: A + 0 = A, A · 1 = A; null element laws: A + 1 = 1, A · 0 = 0.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Idempotent laws: A + A = A, A · A = A; complement laws: A + Ā = 1, A · Ā = 0.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Commutative: A + B = B + A, A · B = B · A; Associative: (A + B) + C = A + (B + C).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Simplify: A + A·B | Q: Apply De Morgan's law to (A·B)'. | Q: Simplify: A·Ā

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A + A·B = A (absorption law). | (A·B)' = A' + B' (De Morgan's first law). | A·Ā = 0 (complement law: a variable ANDed with its complement is always 0).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When applying De Morgan's laws, break the bar, change the operator: AND becomes OR and vice versa. On K-maps, always use Gray code ordering of variables along rows and columns. Group the largest possible power of 2 to obtain the simplest expression. Show each simplification step and state the law used (absorption, distribution, etc.). Every 1 on the K-map must be included in at least one group for SoP form.
